highlights: ByteDance Seed introduced Seedream 5.5 with pixel-level preservation of unedited regions, native RGBA generation, and improved small-text rendering across 100 rounds of editing.
Meituan's LongCat-2.5 is a 1.6T native multimodal MoE model for long-horizon agentic tasks, and NetEase open-sourced Confucius4-R2T2, a stable-prefix streaming ASR model built on Qwen3-ASR-1.7B.
Anthropic reports Claude Fable 5.2 designed three electronic devices whose working prototypes Diode Computers built from its files.

items.title: ByteDance Seed introduces Seedream 5.5 image model
items.summary: Seedream 5.5 preserves unedited regions at the pixel level across 100 rounds of editing, generates native RGBA images with transparency, and improves realism and dense small-text rendering. The model gives creative teams a way to keep refining one image over successive edits and produces assets usable for layout, compositing, and production.

evidence.quote: More Realistic Images, More Stable Editing Across 100 Rounds | Introducing Seedream 5.5 More Realistic Images, More Stable Editing Across 100 Rounds | Introducing Seedream 5.5 Date 2026-11-09 Category Visual Today, we are introducing Seedream 5.5, our next-generation image creation model.

To meet these needs, Seedream 5.5 brings three key upgrades: More stable multi-turn editing: Preserve unedited regions at the pixel level and eliminate color shifts in those areas, while reducing detail loss and image degradation across successive edits.
This supports continued work on the same image across 100 rounds of editing.
Native RGBA assets with transparent backgrounds: Directly generate images with an alpha channel, including full and partial transparency.

More realistic images and clearer text: The model renders lighting, materials, and skin textures more naturally and reduces excessive gloss and overexposure, bringing generated images closer to real photos.
Text rendering also improves significantly, with more accurate rendering of complex character shapes and densely arranged small text.
Compared with other major models, Seedream 5.5 achieves leading results in text structure and text-to-image realism.
To address this, Seedream 5.5 uses targeted training to preserve unedited regions at the pixel level, enabling creative teams to keep refining an image through successive edits.
Seedream 5.5 introduces native RGBA generation, directly producing images with an alpha channel that supports full and partial transparency.
The model preserves the subject's shape and texture while accurately rendering edges and transparent regions, so the output can be used as a standalone asset in layout, compositing, and production.
Seedream 5.5 improves the generation and layout of densely arranged small text, reproducing complex character shapes more accurately.

items.title: Meituan publishes LongCat-2.5 multimodal MoE model
items.summary: LongCat-2.5 is a native multimodal MoE model with 1.6 trillion total parameters and approximately 48 billion activated per token, combining visual understanding with agentic coding for complex codebase development, full-project builds, creative design, and 3D tasks. It applies W4A4 quantization to expert weights and activations for native INT4 computation on domestic AI accelerators and can be deployed on NPU platforms.

evidence.quote: meituan-longcat / LongCat-2.5 Like 64 Follow LongCat 5.43k Image-Text-to-Text Safetensors pro_v multimodal text-generation mixture-of-experts agentic conversational custom_code arxiv: 2603.27538 arxiv: 1909.07606 License: mit Model card Files Files and versions xet Community 1 Copy to bucket LongCat
LongCat-2.5 is a native multimodal MoE model for long-horizon agentic tasks, with 1.6 trillion total parameters and approximately 48 billion activated per token .
Building on LongCat-2.0, it combines visual understanding with agentic coding for complex codebase development, full-project builds, creative design, and 3D tasks.
Native Visual Modeling: Building on LongCat-Next , native-resolution visual features are converted into discrete tokens and jointly aligned with text in a shared semantic space.
LongCat-2.5 applies W4A4 quantization to expert weights and activations, enabling native INT4 computation on domestic AI accelerators.
LongCat-2.5 can be deployed on NPU platforms.
For NPU deployment, please refer to SGLang-FluentLLM .

items.title: Anthropic tests Claude Fable 5.2 on electronics design
items.summary: Anthropic asked Claude Fable 5.2 to design three electronic devices — a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub, and a handheld virtual pet — with minimal prompting, and Diode Computers built working prototypes from the files without fixes to the circuitry. The prototypes remain early, so Anthropic does not yet know how they will hold up with continued use or whether they would pass commercial certifications; on the internal PCB Gym benchmark, Fable 5.2 scored 69% compared with 25% for Fable 5.

evidence.quote: next steps Published Nov 9, 2026 Team Science A little over a year ago, we began testing how well Claude could design basic electronic circuits.

To see how newer Claude models have improved in this area, we collaborated with Diode again, this time asking Claude Fable 5.2 to design three electronic devices: a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub, and a handheld virtual pet.
With minimal prompting, Claude was able to use geometric reasoning to lay out each circuit board, anticipate manufacturing constraints, and make sure its designs would work within them.
It revised its own work, modeled its designs in computer-aided design (CAD) software, and, finally, directed human engineers to build prototypes that worked without any fixes to their circuitry.
Diode assembled the circuit boards and ran the firmware, under Claude’s direction.
The final result was a prototype of a speakerphone that still works after weeks of use.
Because the devices are early prototypes, we don’t yet know how they’ll hold up with continued use or whether they would pass commercial certifications.

To demonstrate how much better Fable 5.2 is than earlier models at laying out circuit boards, we asked Diode to run PCB Gym—an internal benchmark that scores models based on how well they can place components and reroute connections on board designs whose layouts have been removed.
Fable 5.2 scored 69% on the benchmark, compared with 25% for Fable 5 (Figure 2).
It also performed better on BenchCAD 2.1 , a public benchmark that tests whether models can rebuild 3D parts, assemblies, and circuit boards from engineering drawings and rendered images.
Fable 5.2 scored 83.5%, nearly double the score of its predecessor, Claude Fable 5.1.

items.title: Codex adds opt-in SSH agent forwarding for remote sessions
items.summary: A closed pull request proposed an opt-in codex app-server proxy --forward-ssh-agent mode that refreshes a stable forwarded-ssh-agent.sock symlink so detached app-servers can follow the current proxy connection across SSH reconnects. The author found that in the built-in daemon path the refresh is never observed, because command execution rebuilds child environments from the app-server process environment and keeps using the stale startup socket.

evidence.quote: [codex] Refresh SSH agent for app-server proxy - # 28131 # 28131 Closed abhinav-oai wants to merge 1 commit into main openai/codex:main from codex/forward-remote-ssh-agent openai/codex:codex/forward-remote-ssh-agent Copy head branch name to clipboard Conversation Commits 1 ( 1 ) Checks Files changed
A long-running app-server can retain the SSH_AUTH_SOCK path from the SSH session that launched it.
Once that session exits, the path points to a deleted socket even though the current proxy connection has a live forwarded agent.
Add an opt-in codex app-server proxy --forward-ssh-agent mode.
The proxy validates its inherited agent socket and atomically refreshes a stable forwarded-ssh-agent.sock symlink beside the app-server control socket.
A detached app-server launched with that stable path can therefore follow the current proxy connection across SSH reconnects without changing turn or command execution behavior.

In the built-in daemon path, this refresh is never observed: PidBackend::command_args launches codex app-server --listen unix:// and command_env does not set SSH_AUTH_SOCK , while app-server command execution rebuilds child envs from the app-server process env via create_env .
So for users of codex app-server daemon bootstrap/start whose daemon inherited an old SSH session, --forward-ssh-agent updates the symlink but subsequent commands still use the stale startup socket.
Closing this pull request because it has had no updates for more than 14 days.

items.title: NetEase open-sources Confucius4-R2T2 streaming ASR model
items.summary: Confucius4-R2T2 is a stable-prefix streaming ASR model that never modifies its earlier output while maintaining high accuracy and low latency. It was obtained by post-training Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio with the pre-trained audio encoder and projector frozen, using Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) labels, and its append-only output lets voice agents and simultaneous translators consume text immediately.

evidence.quote: In this work, we present Confucius4-R2T2 (short for Real Real-Time Transcription), a stable-prefix streaming ASR model that never modifies its earlier output while maintaining high accuracy and low latency.
R2T2 is obtained by post-training Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio while freezing its pre-trained audio encoder and projector .
The adaptation is based on the concept of Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) , a new notion that we introduce in this work.
Learning from LSP labels converts a full-context model into a stable-prefix streaming one without any architectural change.
Extensive evaluations show that R2T2 brings streaming recognition close to the base model's full-context quality while delivering stable text with low emission lag .
We open-source the model weights and code at https://huggingface.co/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2 and https://github.com/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2.

Unlike conventional streaming ASR systems that repeatedly revise partial transcripts, R2T2 produces append-only, stable text that downstream systems such as voice agents and simultaneous translators can consume immediately.
The key idea is Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) supervision, which enables us to transform a full-context ASR model into a streaming one through post-training, without architectural modifications.

Built on Qwen3-ASR-1.7B, R2T2 achieves near-offline recognition accuracy with low emission latency, supports configurable streaming chunk sizes, and demonstrates promising cross-lingual generalization.

items.title: SplatAnything normalizes Gaussian spacing for feed-forward 3DGS
items.summary: SplatAnything introduces Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm), which canonicalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing so feed-forward 3DGS methods get a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction. The authors also build a benchmark spanning diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and extrapolated viewpoints, and report state-of-the-art performance with strong gains under substantial variation in scene scale and viewpoint.

evidence.quote: Generated by deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash We identify a key limitation of existing feed-forward 3DGS methods: Gaussian attributes are typically predicted in a radial-distance-normalized space that canonicalizes a global radial statistic of the reconstructed geometry, while the spacing between nei
ghboring Gaussian centers can still vary substantially across scene scale s and camera configurations .
This mismatch induces systematic shifts in Gaussian-scale targets , leading to ambiguous supervision.

To address this, we propose SplatAnything with Gaussian Spacing Normalization ( GSNorm ), which canonicalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing to provide a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction.
To rigorously assess our method, we further establish a systematic benchmark spanning diverse datasets, input sparsity levels , and challenging extrapolated viewpoints .
Extensive experiments demonstrate that SplatAnything achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly strong gains under substantial variations in scene scale and viewpoint.
SplatAnything is v3 of the InfiniSplat series .
From everyday objects and human subjects to expansive aerial scenes, SplatAnything transforms simple captures into 3D Gaussian scenes.
It also supports Rig-Recon for autonomous driving and Pano-Recon for AR/VR, enabling 3D reconstruction from multi-camera rigs and 360° panoramas.

items.title: P^2-MOPD speeds up multi-teacher on-policy distillation
items.summary: P^2-MOPD jointly optimizes the mixing coefficients and the student weights under the same on-policy distillation objective, keeping the student trainable so experts act as parameter priors. Across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales it reaches MOPD's final average recovery in half the training steps, and its 1.7B model reaches 94.7% average recovery versus 80.9% for MOPD.

evidence.quote: Generated by deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Multi-teacher on-policy distillation consolidates expert capabilities by supervising student-generated trajectories , whereas task arithmetic offers a training-free alternative through linear parameter combinations .

We view the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a single differentiable model and propose P^2-MOPD , which jointly optimizes the mixing coefficients and the student weights under the same on-policy distillation objective .

Unlike task arithmetic , which stays within the span of the frozen student and expert parameters for any choice of merging coefficients , P^2-MOPD keeps the student trainable, so the experts act as parameter priors without confining it to this span.

Across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales, P^2-MOPD achieves faster and more balanced recovery than MOPD from the same initialization, surpassing its final average recovery in half the training steps.
At the end of training, our 1.7B model reaches 94.7% average recovery, versus 80.9% for MOPD .

P²-MOPD writes every student module as its own learnable weights plus a weighted sum of the frozen expert task vectors (expert minus base model), and trains the weights and the mixing coefficients α jointly under the same MOPD loss.
The two channels, student weights and coefficients, share one backward pass, α is folded into the weights, and the trained model is a standard checkpoint with no change at inference.
Higher final recovery: 94.7% vs 80.9% (1.7B) and 94.9% vs 83.1% (4B).
Balanced recovery: worst-domain recovery rises from 32% / 47% to 88% / 89%, and the across-domain std falls from 28 / 22 to about 5.

items.title: Video-Coder trains an agentic coding model for video generation
items.summary: Video-Coder autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene, or Draft Video, that supplies structure and motion signals to downstream video generators. The authors curate Video-Coder-SFT-6k and Video-Coder-RL-2k, build a harness integrating code execution, 3D scene rendering, and execution feedback, and train with SFT followed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent , which autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene ( Draft Video ) that provides structure and motion signals to downstream video generators .

To support this paradigm, we design a dedicated data pipeline and curate two high-quality datasets, Video-Coder-SFT-6k and Video-Coder-RL-2k , which contain diverse prompts and ground-truth reference videos .
We further develop the Video- Coder Harness, a unified interactive environment integrating code execution , 3D scene rendering , and execution feedback for agent training and inference .
We then train Video-Coder with SFT fol- lowed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback , which combines execution-based and video-based rewards .
Additionally, we design an annealing training strategy that gradually reduces the execution reward over time, allowing the model to rely more on the video reward in the later training stages.

In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent, which autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene (Draft Video) that provides structure and motion signals to downstream video generators.

To support this paradigm, we design a dedicated data pipeline and curate two high-quality datasets, Video-Coder-SFT-6k and Video-Coder-RL-2k, which contain diverse prompts and ground-truth reference videos.
We further develop the Video- Coder Harness, a unified interactive environment integrating code execution, 3D scene rendering, and execution feedback for agent training and inference.
We then train Video-Coder with SFT fol- lowed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback, which combines execution-based and video-based rewards.

items.title: LongBanana benchmarks long-context multi-reference image synthesis
items.summary: LongBanana is an expert-designed and expert-verified benchmark whose 90 tasks require retrieving dispersed visual evidence, rejecting distractors, and composing one coherent image from multiple references. Each task includes about 32 reference images, 20 constraints, and 50 evaluation items, yielding 4,670 expert-specified atomic evaluation items, and a 15% double-labeled subset shows 89.4% exact agreement and 0.83 quadratic weighted kappa.

evidence.quote: Generated by deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash We introduce LongBanana, to our knowledge the first expert-designed and expert-verified benchmark for long-context multi-reference image synthesis in the age of agent-driven image generation .
The task requires retrieving dispersed visual evidence, rejecting distractors, binding entities and relations, and composing one coherent final image from multiple references.

LongBanana contains 90 carefully designed tasks organized by a 3-by-3 taxonomy; each task includes about 32 reference images, 20 constraints, and 50 evaluation items, yielding 4,670 expert-specified atomic evaluation items in total.

Its graph-grounded evaluation design instantiates each task with reference images and an entity-relation graph , then converts node, edge, and whole-graph obligations into checklist items for Content Fidelity , Relational Binding , and Global Constraint Satisfaction .
Reviewed expert labels include a 15% double-labeled subset with 89.4% exact agreement and 0.83 quadratic weighted kappa.

We further introduce LongBanana-Gen , an agent-harness framework for long-horizon image generation ; experiments show that minimal agent harnesses improve over direct generation, while a ReAct-Plan-Exec-Reflect (RPR) workflow yields harness-dependent gains by strengthening evidence grounding and rep
Together, LongBanana provides an auditable testbed for measuring dense visual evidence use and a shared target for developing stronger agent-driven image-generation systems.
Code and data are available at the project page: https://long-banana.com/.

items.title: EvoWorld links a VLM brain to a video renderer
items.summary: EvoWorld is a brain-renderer collaboration framework in which a vision-language model observes generated segments, maintains an evolving account of the world, and reasons about plausible state transitions, while a segment-autoregressive video renderer realizes them visually. The paper also introduces EvoWorld-Data and EvoWorld-Bench, and the authors report substantially improved event-conditioned causal evolution over recent models while preserving visual quality and consistency.

evidence.quote: Coherent world evolution requires more than visual fidelity: when an event occurs, a model must infer its consequences for the entities in the world and then render the resulting state.

Existing diffusion-based video models lack an explicit mechanism for maintaining world state and reasoning over such event-conditioned consequences , often producing visually plausible but behaviorally static or causally inconsistent outputs.

To make this reasoning gap concrete and measurable, we propose a new problem, Out-of-Sight Causal Evolution , which requires a model to render an event, reason about its consequences for the evolving world state , and reveal a causally plausible outcome as the world continues to evolve, even out of

As a baseline reference solution, we introduce EvoWorld , a brain-renderer collaboration framework in which a vision-language model serves as the world brain: it observes generated segments, maintains an evolving account of the world, and reasons about plausible state transitions, while a segment-au
toregressive video renderer realizes them visually.
We further introduce EvoWorld-Data and EvoWorld-Bench for training and evaluating event realization , causal reactions , and revisit consistency .

Experiments show that EvoWorld substantially improves event-conditioned causal evolution over recent models while preserving visual quality and consistency, establishing a reference point for reasoning-guided, autonomous world evolution beyond the current field of view.
EvoWorld combines a VLM brain with a visual renderer, enabling off-screen entities to remain active participants in an evolving world.
Within a bidirectional autoregressive paradigm, EvoWorld supports event-triggered world evolution, subject and scene revisitation, and out-of-sight dynamics rendering through model reasoning.

items.title: A2-MEAS uses correction codes for embodied agents
items.summary: A2-MEAS is an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface, where learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals, and MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. On all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 public tasks it reaches a 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success, and across 12 real-robot tasks in five household settings A2-WLA achieves 57.92% average success versus 26.67% for pi0.5.

evidence.quote: We introduce A2-MEAS , an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface.
Learned correction codes combine corrective language , spatial evidence , execution history , and action proposals .
MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance .
A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment.
The action model , A2-WLA , adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy .
On all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 public tasks, A2-MEAS achieves 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success.
On RoboTwin 2.0, A2-WLA achieves 93.98% average success, rising to 95.05% with the complete system.
Across 12 real-robot tasks in five household settings, A2-WLA achieves 57.92% average success versus 26.67% for pi0.5.
We will release the system, models, training scripts, and infrastructure to support efficient embodied learning .

items.title: PCBRouteAgent routes boards with global planning and KiCad
items.summary: PCBRouteAgent pairs a Global Routing Planner that sets connection topology, routing order, corridors, and layer transitions with a Detailed Routing Executor that realizes those guides through KiCad's native routing engine and performs bounded local recovery. On 247 synthetic and real-world boards from four PCBWorld-Bench test splits it posts clean-pass rates of 100%, 94.9%, 100%, and 40% on D2, D3-A, D3-B, and D3-C.

items.title: LowRAM compresses the KV cache at test time
items.summary: LowRAM pairs value cache amortisation, which fits a lightweight per-head predictor at test time and stores residuals only for poorly reconstructed tokens, with cross-layer low-rank key compression. The pipeline keeps decoding overhead minimal and reaches up to 5times higher peak decode throughput at 4times compression, and with quantisation and eviction it reaches 26.9times compression at 94.5% of baseline performance on long contexts.

evidence.quote: We identify a complementary axis: within each attention head , values are largely predictable from their corresponding keys.

We exploit this with value cache amortisation , which fits a lightweight per-head predictor at test time and stores residuals only for the tokens it reconstructs worst, giving 4times near-lossless value compression .
The predictor can be initialised by meta-learning for substantially reduced prefill overhead , or fitted from scratch in settings that allow a one-off cost, such as multi-query inference .
We pair value amortisation with cross-layer low-rank key compression to produce LowRAM , an asymmetric compression pipeline that stays close to lossless across three model families.
By reconstructing only a selected subset of KV pairs at each decoding step , LowRAM can keep decoding overhead minimal and achieve up to 5times higher peak decode throughput at 4times compression.
LowRAM further composes with quantisation and eviction , reaching 26.9times compression at 94.5% of baseline performance on long contexts.
This achieves 4× value-cache compression with near-lossless performance.
With selective reconstruction, we also reach up to 5× higher peak decode throughput at 4× KV compression on at 262K context!
Combining all three lets us push compression to 26.9×, while retaining 94.5% of baseline performance.

items.title: FinDendro benchmarks temporal self-knowledge in LLMs
items.summary: FinDendro contains 2,226 dated U.S. facts from 1999 to 2026, covering monthly macroeconomic series, month-end stock prices, and Federal Reserve decisions, with controls for persistence and dominant outcomes that keep chance accuracy near 0.27. GPT-5 answers 76% of controlled facts correctly but claims to know 38%, so backtests inside a model's training window cannot be certified leak-free by self-report, instruction, or stated cutoff.

evidence.quote: To verify whether any of these safeguards can be trusted, we introduce FinDendro, a benchmark of 2,226 dated U.S.
facts from 1999 to 2026, covering monthly macroeconomic series, month-end stock prices and Federal Reserve decisions.
Results show that for most frontier models , self-reports understate knowledge.
GPT-5 answers 76% of controlled facts correctly but claims to know 38%, and answers 61% of the facts it says it does not know.
Knowledge claims can persist beyond the measured knowledge boundary, by up to seven quarters, and a declared date removes most of the claims of prior knowledge while leaving accuracy unchanged.
Backtests inside a model's training window therefore cannot be certified leak-free by self-report, instruction or stated cutoff.

These findings motivate behavioral measurement of temporal knowledge boundaries , and FinDendro provides a benchmark and procedure for selecting backtest periods based on demonstrated factual knowledge.

items.title: sentinel-eval reproduces ACL leaks in agent memory writes
items.summary: An offline reproduction harness tests whether metadata filters like allowed groups still protect shared collections when agents summarize documents across folders: ChromaDB and LlamaIndex filters catch 100% of unauthorized raw chunk queries, but parent ACLs are dropped on synthesized notes. In the reported run, direct RAG exposed 0 of 18 restricted chunks while 2 of 3 synthesis tasks leaked sensitive data, and the author notes that strict intersection fixes the leak but destroys multi-source utility.

evidence.quote: Deterministic benchmark and linter for derived-context ACL leaks in agent memory.
Document permissions work for raw RAG (0% leaks).
They silently evaporate in agent memory: our benchmark demonstrates that cross-document synthesis leaks confidential parent secrets in 2 out of 3 background tasks (67%).
ChromaDB and LlamaIndex metadata filters catch 100% of unauthorized raw chunk queries.
But when agents synthesize notes across files into shared memory, parent ACLs are dropped, letting unprivileged users retrieve executive data.
Benchmark Scorecard
Both reference pipelines run the same 24-document corpus, ACL map, personas,
and three scoped synthesis tasks with deterministic local embeddings and a
Derived artifact failure rate: 2/3 = 66.7% .
Raw chunks retrieved: 18 (restricted: 0) -> PASS (0.0% leak)
Artifacts leaking: 2/3 (66.7%)
Leaked restricted canaries: 6/18 (33.3% corpus-wide)
for the same reason: the artifact is authorized by its own metadata, and that
metadata has no source restrictions.
Why Naive Fixes Fail
Strict intersection
destroys multi-source utility.
Authorization belongs at the data layer.

items.title: Twindex proves when data cannot identify a parameter
items.summary: Twindex finds parameter sets that fit the same data and writes an exact certificate that a small standard-library Python checker with no floating point replays, returning VALID, INVALID, or INCONCLUSIVE. It covers ODE models, PDEs in one and two dimensions and in time, and works on any simulator you can call from Python as a clearly labelled numerical audit.

evidence.quote: Your inverse solver returned a parameter.
Twindex proves whether the data could have determined it.
Least squares, Bayesian inference and physics-informed neural networks will
Twindex finds such twins and proves it: it writes an exact
certificate that a small checker, standard-library Python with no floating
point, replays and verifies.
It works on ODE models (epidemics, pharmacokinetics, chemical kinetics, ecology,
neuron models), on PDEs in one and two dimensions and in time, and, as a clearly
labelled numerical audit, on any simulator you can call from Python.
A pair proves that the data cannot
determine a parameter better than $\pm L/2$ .
The checker, about 5,700 lines of
standard-library Python and type-checked with mypy --strict , gives one of
VALID : the claim is proved;
INVALID : the certificate is malformed or its claim is false;
INCONCLUSIVE : nothing was proved either way.
